operation_tail.detail: Spring 2026 received fixed-coverage submissions from 52 fixed-network providers; this provider count is provenance metadata, not a candidate count.
Spring 2026 received submissions from 18 fixed-wireless-access providers and keeps them distinct from fixed-network providers.
Provider submissions cover premises where an end-user could order a fixed broadband service; planned-only locations are not included as current availability.
All fixed coverage and active full-fibre line values in this data package are bound to the January 2026 snapshot.
The package publishes fixed coverage at UK/nation, local-authority, constituency, census-output-area and postcode levels; levels are not interchanged.
Full-fibre take-up uses active broadband connections serving residential or business customers, not network-passed premises.
The January 2026 coverage assessment uses Ordnance Survey AddressBase Premium and Islands Epoch 123 as its premise base.
The data is released on an open basis under the Open Government Licence, subject to its conditions.
Official files are CSV and use double-quote text delimiters where applicable; parsing must preserve quoted text.
The UK-and-nations fixed coverage file is documented with exactly 495 data rows.
The Location field is restricted to UK, England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
The Premise type field distinguishes All, Residential and Commercial rather than inferring type from postcode.
The Rurality field uses Total, Urban and Rural as explicit categories.
The UK-and-nations file uses documented categories including premise base, unclassified, threshold bands, full fibre and gigabit capable.
The % Premises field represents the percentage of premises covered and is not a count or measured speed.
The Premises field represents the number of premises covered and is kept separate from percentage fields.
The Date field is documented as Jan-26 in Mon-YY format; it is not parsed as a daily observation.
The local/unitary-authority full-fibre take-up file is documented with exactly 361 data rows.
Local-authority full-fibre take-up combines residential and business active connections.
Take-up as a percentage of full-fibre coverage uses all premises with full-fibre coverage as the denominator.
Take-up as a percentage of all premises uses the complete local-authority premise base as the denominator.
A take-up percentage can fall when coverage grows faster than active lines, even when the active connection count increases.
Detailed fixed coverage is provided at five explicit levels: local authority, Westminster constituency, devolved constituency, output area and postcode.
Each detailed geography level has all-premises and residential-only variants; they are not merged.
The all-premises local-authority fixed coverage file is documented with 361 rows.
The residential local-authority fixed coverage file is documented with 361 rows.
The all-premises Westminster constituency fixed coverage file is documented with 650 rows.
The residential Westminster constituency fixed coverage file is documented with 650 rows.
The all-premises devolved constituency fixed coverage file is documented with 131 rows.
The residential devolved constituency fixed coverage file is documented with 131 rows.
The all-premises census output-area fixed coverage file is documented with 238,878 rows.
The residential census output-area fixed coverage file is documented with 238,850 rows.
Output-area geography uses the 2021 census for England, Northern Ireland and Wales and the 2022 census for Scotland.
Full-fibre coverage is not reported at output-area or postcode level because of commercial confidentiality; no value is synthesized.
Coverage fields refer to fixed-line broadband unless FWA is explicitly named in the field description.
Postcode files contain an explicit postcode-area field, such as SE, which must agree with the member file area.
The All Premises count field is present at all detailed levels except postcode and must not be fabricated for postcode rows.
The All Matched Premises count field is absent from postcode files and is not inferred from coverage percentages.
A matched premise requires at least one fixed-provider record with a non-zero predicted download speed.
Premises not matched to a qualifying provider record are classified as unclassified rather than assigned zero coverage by inference.
SFBB availability is the percentage of premises covered at 30 Mbit/s download or greater.
UFBB (100 Mbit/s) availability is the percentage of premises covered at 100 Mbit/s or greater.
UFBB availability without the 100M label is defined at 300 Mbit/s or greater.
The Full Fibre availability field is restricted to local-authority and constituency files and is absent from output-area and postcode files.
Gigabit availability is a percentage field supplied across all detailed geography levels, including postcode.
Unable-to-receive percentages use matched premises and documented thresholds of 2, 5, 10 and 30 Mbit/s.
The unable-to-receive-decent field includes unmatched records and zero predicted speeds and considers fixed, WISP and Mobile FWA routes.
NGA includes active fixed-line technologies other than ADSL, including full fibre, HFC, VDSL and G.Fast.
Maximum-download-speed percentages use the documented bands 0-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-30, 30-300 and at least 300 Mbit/s.
Fifty official provider-scope, snapshot, geography, row-count, denominator and field-semantics controls were published line by line; candidate promotion remains blocked pending strict r2 bytes.
